capacity-planning.name: Capacity Planning
capacity-planning.summary: Workforce and operational capacity-planning arc: kickoff, urgency, current state, projection, tactics, implementation, revision, conclusion. For decks where leadership must decide whether the organization has enough resources to meet upcoming demand.

beats.name: Kickoff
beats.description: Introduce what the planning exercise covers and the decision you need from the audience. Frame the time horizon and the resources in scope so the rest of the deck stays bounded.

beats.name: Urgency
beats.description: Show why this is the right moment to plan capacity. Pipeline shifts, hiring freezes, operational stress signals. Urgency turns capacity from an annual ritual into a decision the audience leans into.

beats.name: Situation
beats.description: Highlight the current resource picture: people, tools, infrastructure, vendor capacity. Show utilization, not just headcount. The audience should know where slack and stress live today.

beats.name: Projection
beats.description: Predict future demand under your base case and a sensitivity case. Tie demand to specific drivers — pipeline, launches, seasonality — so the audience can challenge the assumptions, not just the totals.

beats.name: Tactics
beats.description: Suggest the strategies for closing any gap: hiring, automation, outsourcing, prioritization. Each tactic should map to a specific demand driver and a defensible cost.

beats.name: Implementation
beats.description: Discuss how the plan gets deployed. Sequencing, owners, dependencies, lead times. Capacity decisions slip the most when the rollout isn't planned with the same rigor as the sizing.

beats.name: Revision
beats.description: Define the leading indicators that would trigger a re-plan, and the cadence of review. Capacity plans age fast; show the audience how the plan stays alive.

beats.name: Conclusion
beats.description: Wrap up with the specific recommendations and the decisions you need today. End with the next checkpoint and what evidence will be on the table at it.

candidates.name: Candidates
candidates.summary: Potential hires evaluating company, role, and people.
candidates.description: Candidates are weighing a major life decision and have many alternatives. Lead with mission and why-now, show the team they'll work with, and be honest about the stage. Avoid generic recruiting copy — specifics build trust faster than polish.

general-public.name: General Public
general-public.summary: Mixed non-expert audience with no assumed domain knowledge.
general-public.description: A mixed audience of non-experts with no assumed domain knowledge. Prefer analogies to data, use only simple charts, set large text for accessibility, and structure the talk as a story. Keep chart density low; 10-15 slides.

inform.name: Inform
inform.summary: Give the audience clear context, facts, or status without asking for a decision.
inform.description: Use when the deck needs to make the audience aware of current state, background, or findings. Prioritize clarity, completeness, and accurate framing over persuasion.
inform.outcome: The audience understands the situation and can repeat the important facts.
successCriteria: Audience can summarize the key facts
Follow-up questions are about implications, not basic context

formal.name: Formal
formal.summary: Polished, restrained voice for board, investor, and regulator audiences.
formal.description: Authoritative without being cold. Use third-person constructions, full sentences, and concrete numbers. Avoid hedges and humor that depend on shared in-jokes; rely on clarity and precision to land.
voiceCues: Use third person and the corporate 'we' sparingly.
Lead with the recommendation, then evidence.
Quote concrete numbers; avoid round-tripping ranges.
Prefer full sentences to bullet fragments on key claims.
samplePhrases: Q4 revenue grew 18% year over year, led by enterprise expansion.
We recommend approving the Series B raise at $30M.
Net retention was 124%; gross retention was 96%.

minimal.name: Minimal
minimal.description: A clean, minimalistic theme with a focus on simplicity and readability. Ideal for professional, straightforward presentations.

burnt-orange.name: Burnt Orange
burnt-orange.summary: Warm orange and red accents for energetic commercial decks.
burnt-orange.description: A warm, high-contrast palette built around burnt orange, red, navy, and gold. It feels active without losing structure.

cool-horizon.name: Cool Horizon
cool-horizon.summary: Cool blue-green palette tuned for professional business decks.
cool-horizon.description: A balanced cool-toned scheme with deep navy, business blues, and teal accents. It works well across strategy, finance, and technical narratives.

calibri.name: Calibri
calibri.description: Calibri is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Calibri for both headings and body text.

aptos.name: Aptos
aptos.description: Aptos is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Aptos Display for headings with Aptos for body text.

cover.name: Cover
cover.summary: The opening slide: title, subtitle and an optional picture.
cover.description: Open a presentation with its subject and a short introduction. Add a picture when it helps establish the context.

text.name: Text
text.summary: Prose. Several blocks sit side by side when short and stack when long.
text.description: Explain one idea in continuous prose. Use paragraphs or flowing blocks for detail that needs to be read in sequence.

chart.name: Chart
chart.summary: One to six charts, with an optional note.
chart.description: Give a chart enough space to show its evidence. Use the title to state the conclusion and labels to explain the measures.

table-beside.name: Table beside
table-beside.summary: A table with commentary beside it.
table-beside.description: Place a table beside its interpretation. Use the supporting text to explain the conclusion without repeating every cell.

timeline.name: Timeline
timeline.summary: Dated events or a roadmap along one axis, with optional notes.
timeline.description: Show events or milestones in chronological order. Label each item with a date or stage and a concise description.

list.name: List
list.summary: Bulleted or numbered points; one long list flows into columns.
list.description: Present several related points in a clear sequence. Use bullets for independent points or numbered items for an ordered list.
